sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: Aircraft-operator status depends on performing aviation activity and exceeding the applicable full-scope emissions threshold.
Commercial and non-commercial air transport operators have different thresholds.
In-scope aviation activity generally starts with a departure from a UK aerodrome.
In-scope destinations include the UK, EEA states excluding outermost regions, and Gibraltar, subject to excluded-flight rules.
Flights from a UK aerodrome to an offshore structure on the UK continental shelf can be in scope.
Excluded flights are removed from aviation activity scope.
facts.expected_handling: Apply exclusion rules before threshold calculations.

facts.source_fact: Regulator assignment depends on registered office or residence.
METS reporting requirements may be marked exempt where no aviation activity occurred or thresholds were not met.
A regulator may identify exempt status using Eurocontrol data.
An operator should inform its regulator promptly if it believes an exempt status is incorrect.
facts.expected_handling: Route disputed exemption to regulator review.
